Let <MATH_0001> be a scheme. Let <MATH_0002> be an ample invertible
<MATH_0003>-module. Let <MATH_0004> be a morphism of schemes.
Assume at least one of the following conditions holds
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> <MATH_0005> is a quasi-compact immersion,
<STRUCT_0003> <MATH_0006> is quasi-compact and <MATH_0007> is an immersion,
<STRUCT_0004> <MATH_0008> is quasi-compact and induces a homeomorphism
between <MATH_0009> and <MATH_0010>,
<STRUCT_0005> <MATH_0011> is quasi-compact and <MATH_0012> induces a homeomorphism
between <MATH_0013> and <MATH_0014>.
<STRUCT_0006>
Then <MATH_0015> is ample on <MATH_0016>.

Observe that in cases (1) and (3) the scheme <MATH_0001> is quasi-compact
as <MATH_0002> is quasi-compact by Definition <REF_0001>.
Thus it suffices to prove (2) and (4). Since (2) is a special case
of (4) it suffices to prove (4).

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
Assume condition (4) holds. For <MATH_0003>
denote <MATH_0004> the pullback of <MATH_0005> to <MATH_0006>. Note that
<MATH_0007> is a section of <MATH_0008>. By
Proposition <REF_0002>
the opens <MATH_0009>, for <MATH_0010>,
form a basis for the topology on <MATH_0011>. Since <MATH_0012> by
Modules, Remark <REF_0003>
and since <MATH_0013> is a homeomorphism, we conclude
the opens <MATH_0014> form a basis for the topology of <MATH_0015>. Hence
<MATH_0016> is ample by
Proposition <REF_0004>.

Let <MATH_0001> be a quasi-separated scheme. Let <MATH_0002>, <MATH_0003> be schemes over <MATH_0004>.
Let <MATH_0005> be an ample invertible <MATH_0006>-module
and let <MATH_0007> be an ample invertible <MATH_0008>-module.
Then <MATH_0009>
is an ample invertible sheaf on <MATH_0010>.
